items.title: How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule
items.summary: With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to CrimeaAt 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months the work had become almost mundane: they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions. Continue reading...

items.title: Cricket Australia press conference: CEO speaks to media amid ‘sandpapergate’ controversy – live
items.summary: Updates ahead the final ODI in the series at Bellerive OvalPlay start time in Hobart is 2.30pm AEDT/3.30am BSTAny thoughts? Get in touch with an emailWe are indeed very, very proud the culture that this team has built the past eight years. Our players our leaders, our coaches deserve enormous credit for that. In particular Pat and Andrew who continue to lead this team with distinction. But we recognise the pain and the hurt that events surrounding sandpaper have caused. The game is genuinely hurting the moment. It’s not good for anyone. We need to find a path through, we need some time to heal.As of this process, and so all parties who wish to can tell their version of events we have set up now an independent forum, a chance to give everyone a voice in an independent a safe setting. It’s not investigation. It’s not to produce a sanction. No one is forced to participate. It is entirely up to each individual. It’s important to remember we’re talking about events that happened eight a half years ago. And I hope everyone will respect this process the players be afforded the space to at their best at what is a very important time and period for the game.CA CEO Todd Greenberg is ready to speak …For the past week we’ve had several different and conflicting accounts of what occurred in Cape Town in 2018. And it’s an incredibly difficult and uncomfortable time the game and for who was involved. What happened then and continues to play out has a to do with the culture that existed back at the time, a culture that CA played a part in creating. Continue reading...

items.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
items.summary: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

items.title: Keepsake County review – eccentric stealing simulator with a social conscience
items.summary: PC; Forward InstinctThis irreverent stealth game depicts Samuel’s lonely life robbing garish, midwestern abodes – it’s a Shameless way to make a livingFor many people, McMansions are an eyesore, but for the protagonist of Keepsake County, a renowned burglar, they are an enticing opportunity. Prowling at purple-hued dusk, this unfussy thief is just as likely to steal a half-eaten slice of pizza or a naff ceramic ornament as he is an expensive set of golf clubs. It’s a sad, desperate way to make a living, a sense compounded by what this fledgling kleptomaniac carries his loot away in: a plastic shopping bag.Countless works have taken us to breadline America, from classic novel East of Eden to acclaimed TV crime drama Mare of Easttown. But Keepsake County is no prestige examination of the economic underbelly of the US. Rather, it is a stealing simulator with eccentric Adult Swim-style art and a darkly absurdist sense of humour that is expressed in its moment-to-moment action. For example, when I set off the alarm at a glinting modernist abode, I had to quickly dodge the gunshot fired my way by its maniacal owner, and as I scarpered across the surrounding grassy verge, I grabbed underpants off the clothesline just to make the long drive through the night worth it. I was reminded of Shameless (the US version) as much as Steinbeck. Continue reading...
